notes: CONFIRMED from the paper. Single randomised sample of 57 consenting participants assigned to CR+IPS (n=28) and IPS alone (n=29) on the island of Tenerife; one recruited cohort, two allocated arms, no second independently recruited sample.

CONFIRMED from the paper. Five-year follow-up of the baseline IOT randomised trial (Shimada et al. 2018), 136 randomised at six Nagano hospitals, 102 analysed at five years. One recruited cohort. The baseline trial report is a sibling publication of this cohort and is not in the frozen 90-report set under batch F12.

CONFIRMED from the paper. One nationwide Swedish register cohort of 21,551 incident first-episode nonaffective psychosis cases 2006-2016. No participant overlap with parachute_sweden, stockholm_2000 or stockholm_2005; see the cohort overlap_notes.

CONFIRMED from the paper. One recruited sample of 162 first-episode patients at the Parnassia Centre for Early Psychosis, The Hague. The Dutch, second-generation and first-generation groups are a post-hoc split of that single sample by migration background, so under D12.5 they are subgroup arms of ONE cohort, not three cohorts.
CONFIRMED from the paper. The Parachute project cohort, 175 enrolled of 253 eligible FEP cases across 17 Swedish clinics 1996-97, 161 with complete register records at year 13.

CONFIRMED from the paper, with a qualification. The cohort is the 447-person first-diagnosis-2000-2004 subsample of the larger SUPP study of 1,480 persons; the SUPP parent sample is a wider cohort that this report does not analyse. The two reported groups (institutional recovery n=53, ongoing institutionalisation n=159) are post-hoc subgroups defined by service contact during follow-up, not separately recruited cohorts.
